streamed_loading.reported_behavior: The inter-planet loading hitch: the swap frame took 170-225 ms on the main thread (VR_HITCH startup 120-180 ms, unload 13-27 ms, despawn 11-33 ms) and the render thread then stalled about 100 ms uploading the whole level (prep up to 93 ms).
changes: The loader thread prepares the level start beside the load (crate::level_switch::PreparedLevel): the tfrag batches, tie, shrub and moby class meshes, their images, the tie and shrub instance records and entity lists (names included). The boot uses the same path; the title world and Going Commando build theirs in place.

A VR flight streams the destination (crate::level_stream): meshes and images get their handles at the swap and are inserted at most 4 MiB, 12 images and 48 meshes per frame; tie and shrub entities are spawned within 2.5 ms per frame, the tie LOD state naming each instance's entities as they come.

At the swap the old ties are hidden and despawned a few hundred per frame; the level's unloaded resources, the replaced Level, fog and spawn states and the old level's lumps are freed on a cleanup thread (every level change).
The voyage may finish only once the stream is empty and the destination uploaded; a new level change first completes a stream still running.

VR_HITCH stream (what was streamed, frames, job time) and VR_HITCH frame (any main or render frame of 20 ms or more during a transition, with its phase and its time per main schedule); VR_PERF main now includes the level change's frame; `level setup:` times the set-ups of a level's first frame (gameplay step by step, Ratchet's attachments, the menus' 3D models, the vendor).

A flight streaming the destination leaves the gameplay set-up, Ratchet's attachments, the menus' 3D models and the vendor for the cut to the landing, under black; the voyage (travel post_tick), the VR camera (follow_game_camera) and the flight's audio use the departure's play state until then, and the pipeline warm-up view is the level's Ratchet instance.

Lean steering: the neck's sideways offset from where it was when the board was placed (or the view recentred), straight within 4 cm, full turn at 20 cm; VR Options -> Hoverboard lean (vr_board_lean, on by default).

The view follows the board's heading (time constant 0.12 s, at most 4 rad/s), stays anchored at the head's position at the start or respawn (a lean moves the eye), and takes no room-scale step on the board; no snap turn on the board.

Board controls: the right trigger boosts (square), the left grip is L1, the right stick up / right / down / left holds the L1 / R1 / L2 / R2 tricks (the left trigger, X and B still do); the trigger fires no weapon on the board.
A VR landing tilted beyond 60 degrees or turned more than 80 degrees from the board straightens the body along the board instead of throwing Ratchet off; an unfinished trick still does.

player_feedback_fixes.reported_behavior: Player reports: the Decoy Glove's ball not centred in the hand; the hoverboard race start depending on where the player faced; saves that could not be overwritten (the warning showed, its confirm did nothing); a seated / standing option that adjusts the height.
changes: The held Decoy Glove ball (vr::bomb_glove's hold): the decoy's model is not built about its origin; the centre of its drawn pose (the mean of its joints' translations) is put at the palm. A first build used its sequence's bounding sphere, which bounds the whole animation (the inflated decoy included): the headset showed the ball further off than before.

The hoverboard's mount (rc_game::hero::hoverboard's SetState 0x6b entry) in VR: Ratchet's facing is the player's until he mounts (tracked_face), so the board could start where the player faced (Rilgar's headset session: the mount took the player's facing, 3.0 rad, not the start's -2.1); mounted from foot or placed at the start (not from a crash, wall or water state), the board now starts along the race path where it is (the nearest point toward the next, as a respawn), on every level, and the view's existing snap to the board's front follows. Level 5's native start yaw (-2.1) faces back up the course: the original's camera-relative steering turned the board around at once, the VR steering (about the board's heading) kept it (a second headset session: the start at -2.1, the player riding the other way); the start now takes the path's direction there too (VR_GAME board_start logs it). The start set Ratchet's yaw but not his rotation rows, which the ride's slope alignment (align_up) rebuilds the Euler angles from: the next tick turned him back to the player's facing, and the view's snap to the board's front followed it (VR_GAME board_heading logged the player's facing). The rows now follow the yaw; a headset session then logged the view on the course's direction at all four starts.

Enemies the Walloper sparked on without damage, with either hand, standing still (the player's report): the moby loop runs a moby when it was drawn last frame (+0x31) or is within its update distance of the native camera, and VR took +0x31 from the native camera's culls alone. That camera follows behind Ratchet on its own (the headset never turns it), so in a fight on the spot, the player turned or snap-turned toward enemies it did not frame: they stood frozen, their hit records never read, while the lunge's spheres listed them (the sparkles). +0x31 is now also set for what the headset draws (moby_render for the level mobys, gameplay's upload for the created ones), outside a flight's streaming. Found by reading and not confirmed: enemies within reach of a punch are usually within their update distance of that camera too. A later Rilgar session traced every Walloper hit on the biters (class 623): each was listed, recorded and resolved for 3 damage on its first contact (the rest of the lunge in the resolver's cooldown, as in the original), with no hit lost; the report did not reproduce there.

The overwrite confirmation (and the New Game and challenge confirmations): its "Yes" / "No" hints are drawn inside the page's panel, but vr::menu_pointer placed their pointer targets without the panel's offset, so the trigger on "Yes" sent Cross, which the confirmation ignores. The targets now add the panel's offset.

scripts/vr/Run.ps1 -Level <index> (debug, debug-gold and debug-hologuise launches): the debug boot starts on that level (RC_VR_LEVEL, read by vr::game's debug launch, which set Kerwan alone), e.g. -Level 5 for Rilgar's hoverboard race.

vr_comfort_fixes.reported_behavior: Player reports: the VR Options rows are too close to pick one with the pointer; on the hoverboard with the Player body drawn the head does not follow the body, which often passes through the view; enabling Player body Always from the pause menu shows Ratchet's head while paused; the board's view faces where it goes, while a rider stands side-on and looks over a shoulder. Then, with the side-on view: every respawn and start turned the view to where the player already looked (the head turned to see ahead), a stiff neck's worth further, and re-taking the posture took seconds of the race. Then: VR Options must show every row at once, a line's worth apart (a first build showed five, scrolling); the body's arms swept through the view at every board jump; the lean steered the board left whatever the player did.
changes: VR Options shows all its rows in a taller list panel: the menu frames (class 0x472) are skinned to their four corner joints, so moving a panel's bottom corners down (its top ones up for what the screen's bottom leaves no room for) stretches the drawn frame and its rect alike (rc_game::menus::pause::frame::FrameMobys::grow, the drawn pose's corner joints moved the same in menu_render). VR Options' list panel (port::frame_grow, VR_GROW) is 85% taller, its eight rows about as far apart as the camera list's four, without scrolling.

On the hoverboard, with the Player body drawn, Ratchet's arms are collapsed from the shoulders (vr::body::ratchet_play_joints), not only the forearms: the jumps and tricks swung them through the view. The VR hands stay.

The lean steered one way for good: its reference (the neck when the board was placed) followed the neck only within 3 cm of it, so a posture taken after the start (turning side-on to see ahead) read as a full lean that never returned. After each start and respawn the reference now settles on the neck for a second (the lean does not steer meanwhile), then keeps following it, within 3 cm with a 3 s time constant and beyond with 6 s: a held lean turns through a curve, a posture drifts back to straight.

Ratchet's palette (gameplay's upload) is uploaded again when the Player body's in-play mode changes, not only after a tick: in the pause menu no tick runs, so switching to Always drew the body with its head until play resumed.

With the Player body drawn in play, the eye stays on the body's head on a rail and on the hoverboard (vr::game's Rig::root_for no longer anchors the view to the head's room position there): the lean still steers, measured from the same neck reference, but no longer carries the view out of the body.

On the hoverboard the view faces where Ratchet's body does: his stance, the turn of his shoulder line in the ride sequence 0x52 from his idle's (vr::body::stance_yaw, VR_GAME board_stance logs it), is added to the board's heading for the view's snap and follow, and the lean is measured along the board's right as the room sees it (the toes or the heels), not the player's right.

The board's snap (its start and respawns) took the player's body heading estimated that instant (vr::orientation::body_yaw: the head, the shoulder line, the hands' reach and pointing), which follows the head once the player rides looking over a shoulder; the view then turned to the gaze plus the stance. The heading the board was first taken with (eased to the body for two seconds then, the player not yet in a riding posture) is now kept (Rig::board_body) for every later start and respawn; only the board's own heading changes the view. F8 forgets it.
